description: Benchmark for Day 06 — OpenStax Introduction to Python Programming, chapters 4-6 (PDF pages 95-173). Written and split dev/test BEFORE any retrieval run. gold is a list of acceptable alternatives; a hit needs the chunk's page to equal that alternative's page AND the chunk to contain the full evidence_quote (whitespace/case-normalized).
split_rule: Questions were written per chapter; the 6 test questions were chosen up-front so that each chapter is represented and 2 of them use a metadata filter. Test and dev never share an evidence sentence, but leakage risk exists: t06 and dev q07 share gold page 111 (neighbouring paragraphs of section 4.5), and t04 and dev q13 both accept the chapter-5 summary page 143. All questions come from the same book and author style.
filter_rule: filter = {chapter: N} is an ASSUMED user context supplied before retrieval (e.g. the learner says which chapter they are studying). It never contains the gold page or answer.

questions.question: Which values does bool() convert to False?
questions.expected_answer: 0 and the empty string (any non-zero number or non-empty string becomes True).
questions.evidence_quote: True: any non-zero number, any non-empty string • False: 0, empty string

gold.evidence_quote: True: any non-zero number, any non-empty string • False: 0, empty string

questions.question: What goes wrong if I write is_zero = num=0 when I meant to test whether num is zero?
questions.expected_answer: It assigns 0 to both is_zero and num regardless of num's original value; = is assignment, == is comparison.
questions.evidence_quote: is_zero = num=0 will always assign is_zero and num with 0, regardless of num's original value

gold.evidence_quote: is_zero = num=0 will always assign is_zero and num with 0, regardless of num's original value

questions.question: How many spaces per indentation level does the PEP 8 style guide recommend?
questions.expected_answer: Four spaces per indentation level.
questions.evidence_quote: The PEP 8 style guide recommends four spaces per indentation level.

gold.evidence_quote: The PEP 8 style guide recommends four spaces per indentation level.

questions.question: When an if-else statement runs, can both the if body and the else body execute?
questions.expected_answer: No. One and only one of the branches is taken.
questions.evidence_quote: When an if-else statement is executed, one and only one of the branches is taken.

gold.evidence_quote: When an if-else statement is executed, one and only one of the branches is taken.

questions.question: Which operator is the main exception to left associativity, and how is 2 ** 3 ** 4 evaluated?
questions.expected_answer: Exponentiation is right associative, so 2 ** 3 ** 4 is evaluated as 2 ** (3**4).
questions.evidence_quote: Exponentiation is the main exception (noted above) and is right associative: that is, evaluated from right to left. Ex: 2 ** 3 ** 4 is evaluated as 2 ** (3**4).

gold.evidence_quote: Exponentiation is the main exception (noted above) and is right associative: that is, evaluated from right to left. Ex: 2 ** 3 ** 4 is evaluated as 2 ** (3**4).

questions.question: How does Python evaluate a chained comparison such as 10 < x <= 20?
questions.expected_answer: As 10 < x and x <= 20, evaluated from left to right.
questions.evidence_quote: 10 < x <= 20 is evaluated as 10 < x and x <= 20.

gold.evidence_quote: 10 < x <= 20 is evaluated as 10 < x and x <= 20.

questions.question: Why can two separate if statements give a student a double grade curve, and what fixes it?
questions.expected_answer: Separate if statements do not guarantee only one branch is taken, so both can execute; chaining with elif fixes it.
questions.evidence_quote: Two separate if statements do not guarantee that only one branch is taken and might result in both branches being taken.

gold.evidence_quote: Two separate if statements do not guarantee that only one branch is taken and might result in both branches being taken.

questions.question: What precedence do conditional expressions have compared with other Python operations?
questions.expected_answer: The lowest precedence of all Python operations.
questions.evidence_quote: Conditional expressions have the lowest precedence of all Python operations.

gold.evidence_quote: Conditional expressions have the lowest precedence of all Python operations.

questions.question: In a counting while loop, what happens when the step size is negative?
questions.expected_answer: The counter counts in descending order (positive step counts ascending).
questions.evidence_quote: if the step size is a negative number, the counter counts in descending order.

gold.evidence_quote: if the step size is a negative number, the counter counts in descending order.

questions.question: Is the end value included in the sequence produced by range()?
questions.expected_answer: No. The sequence is inclusive of the start and exclusive of the end.
questions.evidence_quote: This integer sequence is inclusive of the start and exclusive of the end of the sequence.

gold.evidence_quote: This integer sequence is inclusive of the start and exclusive of the end of the sequence.

questions.question: When should I prefer a for loop over a while loop, including in nested loops?
questions.expected_answer: When counting with range() or iterating over a container object, including nested situations.
questions.evidence_quote: A for loop is a preferable option in cases where a loop is used for counting purposes using a range() function, or when iterating over a container object, including nested situations.

gold.evidence_quote: A for loop is a preferable option in cases where a loop is used for counting purposes using a range() function, or when iterating over a container object, including nested situations.

questions.question: What is a loop without a termination condition called, and what statement is essential to leave it?
questions.expected_answer: An infinite loop; a break statement is essential to exit it.
questions.evidence_quote: A loop without a termination condition is known as an infinite loop.

gold.evidence_quote: A loop without a termination condition is known as an infinite loop.

questions.question: What does a continue statement do inside a loop?
questions.expected_answer: It skips the remainder of the current loop iteration without exiting the loop entirely.
questions.evidence_quote: A continue statement allows for skipping the execution of the remainder of the loop without exiting the loop entirely.

gold.evidence_quote: A continue statement allows for skipping the execution of the remainder of the loop without exiting the loop entirely.
A continue statement allows for skipping the execution of the remainder of the loop without exiting the loop entirely.

questions.question: Why do functions make code reusable?
questions.expected_answer: The function body can be executed repeatedly with multiple function calls.
questions.evidence_quote: The body of a function can be executed repeatedly with multiple function calls, so a function promotes reusability.

gold.evidence_quote: The body of a function can be executed repeatedly with multiple function calls, so a function promotes reusability.

questions.question: Can a variable created inside a function be used after the function finishes?
questions.expected_answer: No. It has local scope, only exists within the function, and no longer exists after the function finishes executing.
questions.evidence_quote: A variable created within a function has local scope and only exists within the function. A local variable cannot be accessed outside of the function in which the variable was created. After a function finishes executing, the function's local variables no longer exist.

gold.evidence_quote: A variable created within a function has local scope and only exists within the function. A local variable cannot be accessed outside of the function in which the variable was created. After a function finishes executing, the function's local variables no longer exist.

questions.question: What must a function do before it can edit a global variable?
questions.expected_answer: Declare the variable with the global keyword.
questions.evidence_quote: To edit a global variable inside a function, the variable must be declared with the global keyword.

gold.evidence_quote: To edit a global variable inside a function, the variable must be declared with the global keyword.

questions.question: What does PEP 8 recommend about spaces around the = sign?
questions.expected_answer: No spaces around = when indicating keyword arguments and default parameter values.
questions.evidence_quote: The PEP 8 style guide recommends no spaces around = when indicating keyword arguments and default parameter values.

gold.evidence_quote: The PEP 8 style guide recommends no spaces around = when indicating keyword arguments and default parameter values.

questions.question: What is a branch?
questions.expected_answer: A group of statements that execute based on a condition.
questions.evidence_quote: A branch is a group of statements that execute based on a condition.

gold.evidence_quote: A branch is a group of statements that execute based on a condition.

questions.question: In a nested loop, what does the outer loop control?
questions.expected_answer: The number of the inner loop's full executions.
questions.evidence_quote: The outer loop controls the number of the inner loop's full execution.

gold.evidence_quote: The outer loop controls the number of the inner loop's full execution.

questions.question: What value does a function return if it has no return statement?
questions.expected_answer: None, representing no value.
questions.evidence_quote: Functions introduced so far have not had a return statement, which is the same as returning None, representing no value.

gold.evidence_quote: Functions introduced so far have not had a return statement, which is the same as returning None, representing no value.

questions.question: Why shouldn't a list be used as a default parameter value?
questions.expected_answer: Default values are defined only once for the function, so mutable objects such as lists should not be used.
questions.evidence_quote: Default parameter values are only defined once to be used by the function, so mutable objects (such as lists) should not be used as default values.

gold.evidence_quote: Default parameter values are only defined once to be used by the function, so mutable objects (such as lists) should not be used as default values.

questions.question: If a function changes a list argument, does the caller see the change? What about a string argument?
questions.expected_answer: Yes for a list (mutable: changes appear outside the function); no for a string (immutable: the function changes a local copy).
questions.evidence_quote: A mutable object can be modified after creation. A function's changes to the object then appear outside the function. An immutable object cannot be modified after creation. So a function must make a local copy to modify, and the local copy's changes don't appear outside the function.

gold.evidence_quote: A mutable object can be modified after creation. A function's changes to the object then appear outside the function. An immutable object cannot be modified after creation. So a function must make a local copy to modify, and the local copy's changes don't appear outside the function.

questions.question: When does the else block run?
questions.expected_answer: (Loops chapter) A loop else runs after the loop completes without being interrupted by a break statement.
questions.evidence_quote: A loop else statement runs after the loop's execution is completed without being interrupted by a break statement.

gold.evidence_quote: A loop else statement runs after the loop's execution is completed without being interrupted by a break statement.
A loop else is used to identify if the loop is terminated normally or the execution is interrupted by a break statement.

questions.question: When a call mixes positional and keyword arguments, which must come first?
questions.expected_answer: Positional arguments, in the correct order, before any keyword arguments.
questions.evidence_quote: When mixing positional and keyword arguments, positional arguments must come first in the correct order, before any keyword arguments.

gold.evidence_quote: When mixing positional and keyword arguments, positional arguments must come first in the correct order, before any keyword arguments.

questions.question: What does elif stand for and where must it be placed?
questions.expected_answer: Else if; it is part of a chain and must follow an if (or elif) statement.
questions.evidence_quote: An elif (short for else if) statement checks a condition when the prior decision statement's condition is false. An elif statement is part of a chain and must follow an if (or elif) statement.

gold.evidence_quote: An elif (short for else if) statement checks a condition when the prior decision statement's condition is false. An elif statement is part of a chain and must follow an if (or elif) statement.
